tharavad

Tharavad (also spelled Tharavadu) is a Malayalam word for ancestral home, joint family, and root lineage: the traditional multi-generational house and the extended family that shares it. That is the model. Not a product login. A house with keys.

We run a public machine so nerds can have a real Linux box: mess around, deploy something small, break it on purpose, fix it, repeat. Membership is a pull request. After review you get a NixOS microVM under your name, not a shared account on someone else’s machine.

What you get once you are in:

  • ssh you@you.tharavad.xyz from anywhere with a normal key
  • optional public HTTP: declare a port in git, serve on http://you.tharavad.xyz
  • your own guest; your mess stays yours

Why bother: a lot of people still wish they had a box at 13 (or later) and never get past signup walls, credit cards, or the feeling that the useful rooms closed when the forums did. We cannot reverse that. We can keep one house open.

Yes, this site is http:// not https://. That is not a misconfiguration; it is a feature, or at least a feature-length grumble. Longer rant under Notes: On HTTP. SSH still uses real crypto.

TinkerHub bought the iron. We frob the bits, bring guests up, and share the cycles with the community. How to land a shell is on Join. Longer story on About. Notes (rants) on Notes. Stay cool.
